2	  "title": "feat(workspaces): part 2, Move to (NIW2-600)",
3	  "body": "Linear: [NIW2-600](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-600) · **Stacked on #478** (NIW2-599, part 1b). Merge #478 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What it does

"Move to" for workspaces on local folders (ADR 0033): one item, several selected, or a recording with its exports, from the active workspace to another one, keeping the item's identity and never leaving zero copies.

**The mover** (`main/workspaces/move-item.ts`)
- Moves every file an item owns today: the media, `.kaipu/<id>.json`, the thumbnail, the cursor track, the edit project (`.edit.json`, `.edit.meta.json`, `.assets/`) and the webcam track (`.webcam.mp4`).
- Same drive: a hard link to the target name, then the source's unlink. A link never replaces a file, and keeps size and mtime.
- Another drive (or no hard links, or EXDEV): a copy into the target's `.kaipu/tmp/move-<id>/`, its sha256 compared with the source's, then placed. A mismatch leaves the source untouched.
- The target record is written first: it reserves the stem (`Name (2)` on a collision), so the media never lands before its sidecar.
- Tags remap by slug. A tag the destination does not have is created there with the same name and color.
- A journal in `userData/workspace-moves/` is only a hint. At startup, and before each group, healing looks at both disks and rolls forward or back. It never deletes the only verified copy; a case it cannot prove is kept and logged.
- It refuses, changing nothing:
  - an item whose record cannot be read (`metadataIssue`);
  - a disconnected destination;
  - a destination whose tag registry cannot be trusted;
  - an item dragged out less than 10 s ago;
  - a full drive;
  - a destination that already holds the same `assetId`;
  - anything while a recording or an export runs.

**The item lock.** Session saves, renames, deletes, screenshot overwrites and moves take one lock per item. A session save queued behind a move is refused with `item-moved` and writes nothing.

**Groups.** `workspaces:move-items` runs N single moves one after another. It holds the switch lock (a new `moving` state) from the first item to the last and reports "Moving 3 of 12". A failure does not stop the rest. Stop lets the item in flight finish.

**UI** (design "Kaipu Workspaces v2", section 2)
- An "IN · Work ▾" chip at the right of the header in both editors and on the item page. Its menu shows "Belongs here", then "Move to" with each destination's cost: same drive · instant, other drive · copies, or not connected. The chip is locked, with the reason, while recording, exporting or moving.
- Moving from an editor closes it first. It goes through the same flush and leave guard as a workspace switch.
- Library: a "⋯" menu on every card and row, and a **Select** mode:
  - checkboxes, and shift-click ranges in the order on screen;
  - a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸" with progress and Stop.
  - Every filter stays, and changing one clears the selection. Items that fail stay selected, so a retry is one click.
- Moving a recording that has exports asks "This recording has N exports in Work. Move them too?", with **Move all N+1** or **Move only the recording**.
- The result toast lists what moved, what stayed and why, plus anything not started after Stop. It offers **Switch**.
- When no other workspace exists, the menus offer "New workspace…". It reuses part 1b's dialog and creates or adopts the folder **without switching** (`activate: false`), then moves into it.

## Where the spec and the mock disagreed (the spec won)
- Mock footnote "keeps tags that exist in the destination": the spec and ADR 0033 (decision 7) create missing tags with the same name and color. The footnote now reads "Its tags come along by name."
- Mock "only one workspace · no chevron, no menu": spec decision 19 puts "Move to ▸ New workspace…" in the editors too, so the chip always has a menu.

## Where the code amends ADR 0033 (in the ADR, dated)
- A collision takes ADR 0035's ` (2)` tail, not `<id>-2`. The moved file's name then still follows its title.
- On the same volume the move is a hard link plus unlink, because a `rename` would replace a file at the destination.
- The webcam track (ADR 0037) moves with the item. It is verified by sha256 across drives.

## Not in this PR
- **Synced folders** (decisions 4, 9 and 13). The app does not detect a synced folder yet, so those branches are not built.
- **Cloud-only items and the cloud `workspaceId` step** (part 4). A cloud-only item cannot be checked or moved, and says why.
- **A screen for quarantined moves.** They are kept in `userData/workspace-moves/` and logged at every start.
- **The drag rule in the menu.** A target is not disabled for an item dragged under 10 s ago; the move is refused with that reason instead.

## Review round (Wachiman, pullfrog, CodeRabbit)
- **Healing is stricter about what it deletes.** Rolling a committed move forward now removes the source media and files only while the source is still the moved item: its record carries the same `assetId`, the media still matches the journal, and its edit project is the one that was copied. A source that changed while the target was unplugged is quarantined and left intact; a stem that now belongs to another item is left alone. A source media that cannot be removed keeps its record and the journal, so the file is not listed again under a new identity.
- **Healing no longer empties `.kaipu/drag/`.** It also runs while the app is open, when another item's drag copy may still be read. Startup and quit already sweep it. ADR 0033 decision 11 says so now.
- A failing heal after the commit no longer turns a finished move into an "I/O" failure, and the move reports its real mode (linked or copied).
- A group move that throws reports `stale`, `maintenance` or `io` for what it was; a failed device-id read is not cached; `ensureByName` stops minting tags at the per-item cap.
- The ⋯ menu works from the keyboard: keys pressed inside it no longer open the card or row; focus moves into the menu on open and back on close; select-mode cards expose `aria-pressed`.
- Result toast: a Stop before the first move says nothing moved; exports move in on-screen order; a lost IPC reply says the result could not be read and to check both workspaces.
- Spanish strings say "espacio de trabajo".

## Checks
- `tsc` (node + web), `oxlint` (0 errors), `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 389 files and 4409 tests pass (the final push re-ran the workspace and move suites: 192 tests pass).
- New engine tests run on the real filesystem in temp folders:
  - a crash at every step, linked and copied, then healing leaves exactly one listed, intact copy;
  - the EXDEV branch;
  - a sha mismatch;
  - a collision;
  - the item lock;
  - an unreadable record;
  - tags;
  - a target disconnected while healing.
- **Not run on this machine (by rule):** Electron, Playwright and `/verify`. The app was never launched for this PR, so every UI step below is still unverified on the real app.

## How to test it yourself
Use a copy of your Library, or test items. Before you start, add a second workspace on the internal disk ("Personal").

1. **Same disk.** In the Library, open "⋯" on a recording that has tags and an edit project, then choose Move to ▸ Personal. The row says "Same drive · instant".
   - Expected: it disappears from Work. Switch to Personal: it is there with the same title, tags and edit project, and the editor opens without "missing dependencies".
   - In Finder, nothing named after the item is left in Work's folder or its `.kaipu/`.
2. **USB drive.** Add a workspace on a USB stick (Settings → Workspaces → New workspace… → Use an existing folder…). Move a large recording there. The row says "Other drive · copies".
   - Expected: the toast reports the move, and the file plays from the USB workspace.
3. **Unplugging mid-move.** Move a multi-GB recording to the USB workspace and pull the stick while it copies.
   - Expected: the toast says it stayed in Work with a reason, and the recording still plays in Work.
   - Reconnect and relaunch: exactly one copy is listed, in Work. The stick's `.kaipu/tmp/` holds no `move-…` folder.
4. **Multi-select.** In the Library, click **Select**. Click one card, then shift-click another: everything between them is checked. A cloud-only item cannot be checked.
   - Change a filter chip: the selection clears.
   - Select 5 items, then Move to ▸ Personal. The bar shows "Moving n of 5…" and the toast lists the result. Try **Stop** halfway: the item in flight finishes, and the toast counts the rest as not started.
5. **The exports question.** Export a recording twice. In the Library, move the original.
   - Expected: "This recording has 2 exports in Work. Move them too?"
   - **Move all 3** moves all three. Repeat with **Move only the recording**: the exports stay in Work.
6. **The editor chip.** Open a recording in the video editor. The header's right end shows "IN · Work ▾", and its menu shows "Belongs here" plus each destination's cost.
   - Choose Personal: the editor closes and the recording moves.
   - Start an export and open the chip again: the menu says "Wait for the export to finish" and nothing can be picked.
   - Repeat with a saved screenshot in the image editor.
7. **Keyboard.** Tab to a card's "⋯", press Enter: the menu opens and focus is on the first destination. Press Enter on it: the item moves, and the card does not open. Reopen the menu and press Escape: focus returns to "⋯".
8. **One workspace.** Remove Personal from the list. In "⋯", the only entry is "New workspace…". Create one: the item moves into it, and you stay in Work.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Move recordings, screenshots, and GIFs between workspaces from item pages or the Library. Select multiple Library items, review progress, and stop a group move.
  * Choose whether to move related exports with a recording, or create a new workspace as the destination.
  * View destination availability and drive information, plus reasons an item can’t be moved.
  * Items that fail to move remain selected for another attempt.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved recovery of interrupted moves and prevented workspace switching during an active move.
  * Protected item edits and screenshot overwrites from conflicting with moves.

  "body": "Linear: [NIW2-600](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-600) · **Stacked on #478** (NIW2-599, part 1b). Merge #478 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What it does

"Move to" for workspaces on local folders (ADR 0033): one item, several selected, or a recording with its exports, from the active workspace to another one, keeping the item's identity and never leaving zero copies.

**The mover** (`main/workspaces/move-item.ts`)
- Moves every file an item owns today: the media, `.kaipu/<id>.json`, the thumbnail, the cursor track, the edit project (`.edit.json`, `.edit.meta.json`, `.assets/`) and the webcam track (`.webcam.mp4`).
- Same drive: a hard link to the target name, then the source's unlink. A link never replaces a file, and keeps size and mtime.
- Another drive (or no hard links, or EXDEV): a copy into the target's `.kaipu/tmp/move-<id>/`, its sha256 compared with the source's, then placed. A mismatch leaves the source untouched.
- The target record is written first: it reserves the stem (`Name (2)` on a collision), so the media never lands before its sidecar.
- Tags remap by slug. A tag the destination does not have is created there with the same name and color.
- A journal in `userData/workspace-moves/` is only a hint. At startup, and before each group, healing looks at both disks and rolls forward or back. It never deletes the only verified copy; a case it cannot prove is kept and logged.
- It refuses, changing nothing:
  - an item whose record cannot be read (`metadataIssue`);
  - a disconnected destination;
  - a destination whose tag registry cannot be trusted;
  - an item dragged out less than 10 s ago;
  - a full drive;
  - a destination that already holds the same `assetId`;
  - anything while a recording or an export runs.

**The item lock.** Session saves, renames, deletes, screenshot overwrites and moves take one lock per item. A session save queued behind a move is refused with `item-moved` and writes nothing.

**Groups.** `workspaces:move-items` runs N single moves one after another. It holds the switch lock (a new `moving` state) from the first item to the last and reports "Moving 3 of 12". A failure does not stop the rest. Stop lets the item in flight finish.

**UI** (design "Kaipu Workspaces v2", section 2)
- An "IN · Work ▾" chip at the right of the header in both editors and on the item page. Its menu shows "Belongs here", then "Move to" with each destination's cost: same drive · instant, other drive · copies, or not connected. The chip is locked, with the reason, while recording, exporting or moving.
- Moving from an editor closes it first. It goes through the same flush and leave guard as a workspace switch.
- Library: a "⋯" menu on every card and row, and a **Select** mode:
  - checkboxes, and shift-click ranges in the order on screen;
  - a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸" with progress and Stop.
  - Every filter stays, and changing one clears the selection. Items that fail stay selected, so a retry is one click.
- Moving a recording that has exports asks "This recording has N exports in Work. Move them too?", with **Move all N+1** or **Move only the recording**.
- The result toast lists what moved, what stayed and why, plus anything not started after Stop. It offers **Switch**.
- When no other workspace exists, the menus offer "New workspace…". It reuses part 1b's dialog and creates or adopts the folder **without switching** (`activate: false`), then moves into it.

## Where the spec and the mock disagreed (the spec won)
- Mock footnote "keeps tags that exist in the destination": the spec and ADR 0033 (decision 7) create missing tags with the same name and color. The footnote now reads "Its tags come along by name."
- Mock "only one workspace · no chevron, no menu": spec decision 19 puts "Move to ▸ New workspace…" in the editors too, so the chip always has a menu.

## Where the code amends ADR 0033 (in the ADR, dated)
- A collision takes ADR 0035's ` (2)` tail, not `<id>-2`. The moved file's name then still follows its title.
- On the same volume the move is a hard link plus unlink, because a `rename` would replace a file at the destination.
- The webcam track (ADR 0037) moves with the item. It is verified by sha256 across drives.

## Not in this PR
- **Synced folders** (decisions 4, 9 and 13). The app does not detect a synced folder yet, so those branches are not built.
- **Cloud-only items and the cloud `workspaceId` step** (part 4). A cloud-only item cannot be checked or moved, and says why.
- **A screen for quarantined moves.** They are kept in `userData/workspace-moves/` and logged at every start.
- **The drag rule in the menu.** A target is not disabled for an item dragged under 10 s ago; the move is refused with that reason instead.

## Review round (Wachiman, pullfrog, CodeRabbit)
- **Healing is stricter about what it deletes.** Rolling a committed move forward now removes the source media and files only while the source is still the moved item: its record carries the same `assetId`, the media still matches the journal, and its edit project is the one that was copied. A source that changed while the target was unplugged is quarantined and left intact; a stem that now belongs to another item is left alone. A source media that cannot be removed keeps its record and the journal, so the file is not listed again under a new identity.
- **Healing no longer empties `.kaipu/drag/`.** It also runs while the app is open, when another item's drag copy may still be read. Startup and quit already sweep it. ADR 0033 decision 11 says so now.
- A failing heal after the commit no longer turns a finished move into an "I/O" failure, and the move reports its real mode (linked or copied).
- A group move that throws reports `stale`, `maintenance` or `io` for what it was; a failed device-id read is not cached; `ensureByName` stops minting tags at the per-item cap.
- The ⋯ menu works from the keyboard: keys pressed inside it no longer open the card or row; focus moves into the menu on open and back on close; select-mode cards expose `aria-pressed`.
- Result toast: a Stop before the first move says nothing moved; exports move in on-screen order; a lost IPC reply says the result could not be read and to check both workspaces.
- Spanish strings say "espacio de trabajo".

## Checks
- `tsc` (node + web), `oxlint` (0 errors), `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 389 files and 4409 tests pass (the final push re-ran the workspace and move suites: 192 tests pass).
- New engine tests run on the real filesystem in temp folders:
  - a crash at every step, linked and copied, then healing leaves exactly one listed, intact copy;
  - the EXDEV branch;
  - a sha mismatch;
  - a collision;
  - the item lock;
  - an unreadable record;
  - tags;
  - a target disconnected while healing.
- **Not run on this machine (by rule):** Electron, Playwright and `/verify`. The app was never launched for this PR, so every UI step below is still unverified on the real app.

## How to test it yourself
Use a copy of your Library, or test items. Before you start, add a second workspace on the internal disk ("Personal").

1. **Same disk.** In the Library, open "⋯" on a recording that has tags and an edit project, then choose Move to ▸ Personal. The row says "Same drive · instant".
   - Expected: it disappears from Work. Switch to Personal: it is there with the same title, tags and edit project, and the editor opens without "missing dependencies".
   - In Finder, nothing named after the item is left in Work's folder or its `.kaipu/`.
2. **USB drive.** Add a workspace on a USB stick (Settings → Workspaces → New workspace… → Use an existing folder…). Move a large recording there. The row says "Other drive · copies".
   - Expected: the toast reports the move, and the file plays from the USB workspace.
3. **Unplugging mid-move.** Move a multi-GB recording to the USB workspace and pull the stick while it copies.
   - Expected: the toast says it stayed in Work with a reason, and the recording still plays in Work.
   - Reconnect and relaunch: exactly one copy is listed, in Work. The stick's `.kaipu/tmp/` holds no `move-…` folder.
4. **Multi-select.** In the Library, click **Select**. Click one card, then shift-click another: everything between them is checked. A cloud-only item cannot be checked.
   - Change a filter chip: the selection clears.
   - Select 5 items, then Move to ▸ Personal. The bar shows "Moving n of 5…" and the toast lists the result. Try **Stop** halfway: the item in flight finishes, and the toast counts the rest as not started.
5. **The exports question.** Export a recording twice. In the Library, move the original.
   - Expected: "This recording has 2 exports in Work. Move them too?"
   - **Move all 3** moves all three. Repeat with **Move only the recording**: the exports stay in Work.
6. **The editor chip.** Open a recording in the video editor. The header's right end shows "IN · Work ▾", and its menu shows "Belongs here" plus each destination's cost.
   - Choose Personal: the editor closes and the recording moves.
   - Start an export and open the chip again: the menu says "Wait for the export to finish" and nothing can be picked.
   - Repeat with a saved screenshot in the image editor.
7. **Keyboard.** Tab to a card's "⋯", press Enter: the menu opens and focus is on the first destination. Press Enter on it: the item moves, and the card does not open. Reopen the menu and press Escape: focus returns to "⋯".
8. **One workspace.** Remove Personal from the list. In "⋯", the only entry is "New workspace…". Create one: the item moves into it, and you stay in Work.

content.text: I'm checking that the new `moving` reason type-checks through the relocate path, then I'll finish the review.

findings.title: The new "moving" refusal has no test
findings.body: `relocate-copy.ts:35-36` adds a `moving` branch (`relocateMoving`), and the `explains each remaining refusal` table lists `recording` and `exporting` but not `moving`. Add `[{ ok: false, reason: "moving" }, /Wait for the move/]` so the new string and the switch case are covered. The `default` branch (`relocateFailed`) has no test either.

findings.title: The relocate row says "while a recording or export runs", but a group move now refuses it too
findings.body: `busyNow()` returns `"moving"` while a group move runs (`main/workspaces/index.ts:66-67`). It is wired into the relocate path through `activeTransactionDeps` (`index.ts:343-347`, spread at `index.ts:480`) and checked in `relocateRefusal` (`relocate.ts:24-25`). So `workspaces:relocate` is also refused while a move runs, and the new `relocateMoving` string says so. The spec row, and the matching sentence in `backlog/several-workspaces.md:26`, list only a recording or an export.

contracts.action: Change folder… (workspaces:relocate) is refused with the new reason "moving" while a group move runs
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this diff, `busy: busyNow` was in the relocate-only deps. Switch and relocate now both take it from `activeTransactionDeps()`.
contracts.before_after: Before: `switchWorkspace` and `relocateActive` read `deps.busy()` from `ActiveTransactionDeps` (`switch-transaction.ts:17,88-90,105`). After: `runSwitch` spreads `activeTransactionDeps()` (`index.ts:363`) and `relocateFolder` builds `{ ...activeTransactionDeps(), registry }` (`index.ts:480`), so both get the same `busyNow`, which includes "moving" (`index.ts:66-67`). `relocateRefusal` returns `{ok:false, reason: busy}` before the picker opens (`relocate.ts:24-25`), and `"moving"` is in `WorkspaceRelocateRefusal` (`shared/types/workspaces.ts:158`) and `RelocateOutcome` (`registry.ts:191`).
contracts.visible_effect: `relocateRefusalMessage` maps "moving" to `relocateMoving` (`relocate-copy.ts:35-36`). Both locale files have the key (`en.json:2630`, `es.json:2630`). The user sees "Wait for the move to finish…" instead of the generic `relocateFailed` fallback.
contracts.failure_mode: If a new reason were missing from the switch, the `default` branch shows `relocateFailed` rather than failing silently. `host?.busy() ?? (moveRun ? ...)` falls through correctly, because host `busy()` returns null when idle.

findings.title: The new "moving" refusal has no test
findings.body: `relocate-copy.ts:35-36` adds a `moving` branch (`relocateMoving`), and the `explains each remaining refusal` table lists `recording` and `exporting` but not `moving`. Add `[{ ok: false, reason: "moving" }, /Wait for the move/]` so the new string and the switch case are covered. The `default` branch (`relocateFailed`) has no test either.

findings.title: The relocate row says "while a recording or export runs", but a group move now refuses it too
findings.body: `busyNow()` returns `"moving"` while a group move runs (`main/workspaces/index.ts:66-67`). It is wired into the relocate path through `activeTransactionDeps` (`index.ts:343-347`, spread at `index.ts:480`) and checked in `relocateRefusal` (`relocate.ts:24-25`). So `workspaces:relocate` is also refused while a move runs, and the new `relocateMoving` string says so. The spec row, and the matching sentence in `backlog/several-workspaces.md:26`, list only a recording or an export.

contracts.action: Change folder… (workspaces:relocate) is refused with the new reason "moving" while a group move runs
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this diff, `busy: busyNow` was in the relocate-only deps. Switch and relocate now both take it from `activeTransactionDeps()`.
contracts.before_after: Before: `switchWorkspace` and `relocateActive` read `deps.busy()` from `ActiveTransactionDeps` (`switch-transaction.ts:17,88-90,105`). After: `runSwitch` spreads `activeTransactionDeps()` (`index.ts:363`) and `relocateFolder` builds `{ ...activeTransactionDeps(), registry }` (`index.ts:480`), so both get the same `busyNow`, which includes "moving" (`index.ts:66-67`). `relocateRefusal` returns `{ok:false, reason: busy}` before the picker opens (`relocate.ts:24-25`), and `"moving"` is in `WorkspaceRelocateRefusal` (`shared/types/workspaces.ts:158`) and `RelocateOutcome` (`registry.ts:191`).
contracts.visible_effect: `relocateRefusalMessage` maps "moving" to `relocateMoving` (`relocate-copy.ts:35-36`). Both locale files have the key (`en.json:2630`, `es.json:2630`). The user sees "Wait for the move to finish…" instead of the generic `relocateFailed` fallback.
contracts.failure_mode: If a new reason were missing from the switch, the `default` branch shows `relocateFailed` rather than failing silently. `host?.busy() ?? (moveRun ? ...)` falls through correctly, because host `busy()` returns null when idle.
